title: Stem ginger and oat biscuits
subtitle: chewy oat biscuits with pieces of stem ginger and golden syrup
excerpt: These biscuits have a chewy, slightly sticky centre and a crisp edge, from a combination of rolled oats, golden syrup, and finely chopped stem ginger. They are made by the melting method, where everything goes into one saucepan, which takes about ten minutes. They spread during baking, so leave plenty of space between each.
sourceNotes: Stem ginger and oat biscuit, a British variation on the traditional flapjack/oat biscuit. Method from standard contemporary British home-baking practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: Young ginger root that has been preserved in sugar syrup. It is tender, intensely flavoured, and used in baking for its warm, sweet-hot flavour. Sold in jars.

A biscuit-making method in which the butter and sugar are melted together in a saucepan before adding the dry ingredients. Used for biscuits like ginger nuts and oat biscuits where a chewy texture is wanted.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in an airtight container for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps in an airtight tin for up to 2 weeks. They become chewier after a day.

items.prepNote: finely chopped (about 3 to 4 balls from a jar)

content.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Line two large baking trays with baking parchment.
Melt the butter, golden syrup, and light brown sugar in a medium saucepan over a low heat, stirring, until combined and fluid. Remove from the heat.
Stir in the rolled oats, flour, bicarbonate of soda, and ground ginger until fully combined. Stir in the finely chopped stem ginger.
Roll heaped tablespoons of dough into balls and place on the prepared trays, leaving 6 cm between each. Flatten each ball slightly with the palm of your hand.

Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until golden-brown at the edges. The biscuits will be very soft in the middle when they come out; leave on the tray for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely and crisp up.

attrs.problem: Biscuits spread so much they merge together on the tray
attrs.avoid: Avoid placing too close together; these biscuits spread to about double their original diameter.
attrs.fix: Bake in smaller batches with more space between each biscuit.

attrs.problem: Biscuits very crisp and dry rather than chewy
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-baking; they should be dark at the edges but still look slightly under-done in the very centre.
attrs.fix: Reduce the bake time by 2 minutes next time. Biscuits firm and chew up considerably as they cool.
